subject: Budget range validation - monthly spend band for PayBridge
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Patel <sam.patel@paybridge.com>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-02-25T18:05:00-05:00
Subject: Follow-up: Budget range validation and token volumes

Hi Sam —

Great to meet earlier. Quick recap from today’s discovery and a few asks so we can size pricing and procurement options: 

- Expected monthly token volumes: you mentioned 50M–150M tokens/month for the first 6 months, with a potential spike to ~300M in Q4 if the pilot converts. Can you confirm a realistic steady-state band we should model?
- Target unit economics: do you have an internal target dollars per 1M tokens (e.g., $X / 1M) or an acceptable range we should try to meet?
- Procurement thresholds: what approval level is required for monthly spends in the ranges above (PO only, VP approval, CFO sign-off)? Any PO/contract minimums we should be aware of?

Next steps I propose: I’ll send a quick pricing matrix (per 1M tokens and monthly band assumptions) and a recommended procurement path (monthly usage vs committed reserved capacity) — if you can confirm the steady-state band and who owns procurement we’ll loop them in.

Attaching a preliminary pricing workbook so you have an initial look.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0124

Attachment: redwood-pricing-1Mtokens.xlsx

From: Sam Patel <sam.patel@paybridge.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-02-26T09:12:00-05:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Budget range validation and token volumes

Thanks Marissa — good summary. Quick answers below: 

- Volumes: Pilot (May–Jul): 30M–60M tokens/month. Production steady-state (post-integration): 100M–200M tokens/month. Q4 marketing push could increase to ~350M for 6–8 weeks.
- Target $/1M tokens: We don’t have a hard internal target, but internal stakeholders flagged a target of <$350 per 1M tokens for initial budgeting. If you can show committed pricing that brings us close to that, it will help.
- Procurement thresholds: Anything under $30k/month can be handled by IT procurement with a standard SOW/PO. Over $30k/month requires VP approval; over $75k/month triggers CFO review and a longer procurement cycle (legal + procurement).

Procurement contact is procurement@paybridge.com — please loop them in for formal SOW/PO discussions.

Sam
Senior Product Manager | PayBridge
sam.patel@paybridge.com | (212) 555-6789

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Patel <sam.patel@paybridge.com>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-02-26T14:45:00-05:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Budget range validation and token volumes

Appreciate the details, Sam — super helpful. Based on the bands you provided, here are two starter pricing options (high level) to align with your $/1M target and procurement thresholds: 

1) Usage-based (no commit) — flexible, good for pilot
   - List: $700 / 1M tokens
   - Volume discounts start at 150M+/month (down to ~$420 / 1M)
   - Good if you expect <=100M steady-state initially

2) Committed reserved capacity (6–12 month) — lower unit economics for predictable spend
   - 100M/month commit: $350 / 1M tokens (meets your internal target)
   - 200M/month commit: $300 / 1M tokens
   - Includes 24/7 support SLAs and a 99.9% latency SLO for the dedicated pool

Notes relative to procurement bands you shared: 
- If your steady-state is ~100M/month, a 100M/month committed contract at $350 / 1M would sit right around the $35k/month mark (close to VP approval threshold).
- A 200M commit at $300 / 1M would be ~$60k/month (would require VP approval, but below CFO review).

I’ve attached the pricing workbook with a quick model to show monthly spend vs unit price and a recommended procurement route (pilot -> 6mo commit -> scale). Can you confirm which band you want us to model for a formal SOW? Also, please confirm procurement contact and timeline (typical procurement lead times for those thresholds).

If it helps, Dylan can join a short call with procurement to walk the SOW and timelines — I’ve CC’d him.

Best,
Marissa

Attachment: redwood-pricing-1Mtokens.xlsx

From: Procurement <procurement@paybridge.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Sam Patel <sam.patel@paybridge.com>
Date: 2026-02-27T09:17:00-05:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Budget range validation and token volumes

Hi Marissa / Sam —

Thanks for the summary. We reviewed the pricing bands and have two quick asks before we route for VP approval: 

1) Can you provide a short, one-page SOW that lists the expected monthly commit, cancellation terms, and data handling/security controls (SOC2 + data residency statement)?
2) Can you confirm monthly invoicing cadence and whether a Net-30 or Net-45 term is available for pilot? Procurement prefers Net-30 but can consider Net-45 for new vendors with credit checks.

If the 100M/month committed pricing hits $350 / 1M, that will put us in the VP approval bucket; please include an example invoice and a PO template we can attach to the internal approval.

Procurement Team
PayBridge
procurement@paybridge.com
